figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) identification and verification. (A) Schematic depiction of the ain BGC and homologous clusters conserved across
species of Aspergillus, Penicillium, and Talaromyces. The percent identities of corresponding ain homologs are indicated. Putative functions of ain genes and
homologs: AinA, non-reducing polyketide synthase (NRPKS); AinB, resistance to 7-aminocholesterol (RTA1)-like domain-containing protein; AinC, hypothetical
protein; AinD, C-glycosyltransferase (C-GT); AinE, ABC multidrug transporter; and AinF, highly-reducing polyketide synthase (HRPKS). Starter-unit:ACP
transacylase, KS: ketosynthase, AT: acyltransferase, PT: product template, ACP: acyl carrier protein, TE: thioesterase, DH: dehydratase, ER: enoylreductase, and
KR: ketoreductase. (B) LC–MS analyses of the ain BGC heterologously expressed in A. nidulans (AN). Control strain was transformed with three empty vectors.
ESI, electrospray ionization. TIC, total ion count; (C) LC–MS analyses of biotransformation assays in S. cerevisiae heterologously expressing AinD to determine
C-GT substrate. The chromatograms shown are extracted ion chromatograms (EIC) at the m/z of 1; (D) Schematic of AinD substrate scope as determined in (C).
Depside 4 serves as a substrate for ainD, while 3 does not. The observed degradation product 5 is therefore formed by the hydrolysis of 1, rather than from
the glycosylation of 3 by AinD.
